scope: Splendor core game, 1st edition (2014), complete authoritative extracted/splendor-rules.txt. No expansions or later-edition additions.
composition: Original v1 IDs1-20 unchanged; extension-01-v1 IDs21-36 unchanged; extension-02-v1 IDs37-40 unchanged.

questions.question: Set up a two-player game. How many tokens of each gem color and how many gold tokens remain, how many nobles are revealed, and what happens to unrevealed nobles?
For three players, give the gem-token count per color, gold-token count and noble count. How do those counts differ in a four-player game?
Describe how the development decks and market are prepared: shuffling, order of the three levels, and face-up card counts. Who starts and in which direction does play proceed?
List all four action choices on a turn. May you take gems and then buy a card on the same turn, or reserve and buy that reserved card on that same turn?
What information about tokens you own must be visible to other players, and when?

A green pile contains four tokens; a red pile contains three. Can you take two green, leaving two? Can you take two red? When is the supply threshold checked, and can either gem-taking action take gold?
You begin with nine tokens and take three different gems. Is temporarily holding twelve allowed, how many must you return, can they include the gems just drawn, and does gold count toward the limit?
You have ten tokens and fewer than three reserved cards. You reserve a card while gold is available. What happens to the gold and your token count, and what if the gold supply were empty instead?
From which two places may you reserve a card? If reserving from a deck, which card is taken and is it shown to opponents? Who may eventually buy a reserved card?

You already have three reserved cards and want a fourth, or just want the gold from reserving. Can you reserve now? May you discard or exchange a reserved card to make room, and how can a reserved card leave your hand?

You reserve a face-up level-2 card while that deck has cards left. When and from where is the empty market space refilled? How does this differ when purchasing a face-up card, buying a reserved card, or when the relevant deck is empty?
A card costs two blue and one green. You have two blue bonuses and no green bonus. What tokens must you spend? What if your bonuses cover every required color, and are bonuses spent when used?

A card costs three blue, two black and one white. You have two blue bonuses, one black bonus, and no white bonus; your available payment is one blue token and two gold. Can you buy it? State which costs the tokens cover, where all spent tokens go, and whether your bonus cards stay with you.
Which cards can you purchase with a buy action? After purchase, how should acquired development cards be arranged, and which information on them must always remain visible?

A noble requires three blue, three green and three white bonuses. You have three blue cards, three green cards, two white cards and a white token (or a gold token). Do you qualify? What changes if you instead acquire a third white bonus, and do bonuses above a requirement disqualify you?

At the end of your action you qualify for two nobles. Can you take both, decline all visits, or choose one? Does the visit use another action, how many points does it give, and when is eligibility checked?
Once you receive a noble, where is its tile placed, and is it face up or hidden?

In a four-player game, turns run A, B, C, D, with A first. B reaches fifteen prestige points on their turn. Who still takes a turn before the game ends, does A take another turn, and is B guaranteed to win?

You have thirteen prestige points and receive a noble at the end of your turn. What is your new total, does that trigger the end of the game even though you skipped over fifteen, and when is the winner determined?

At the end, A has sixteen prestige and ten purchased developments; B has sixteen prestige and nine purchased developments plus three cards still reserved; C has fifteen prestige and only five purchased developments. Who wins and why? Do nobles count toward prestige, and do B’s reserved cards count as purchased developments for the tiebreaker?

You have reserved cards showing a total of eight prestige points and two white bonuses, but have not bought them. Do those printed points count toward your score or the 15-point trigger, and do those bonuses reduce purchase costs or satisfy nobles?

You buy a development card with a blue bonus and zero prestige. Do you receive a physical blue token from the supply, does its bonus work for future purchases, and can it help qualify you for a noble despite being worth zero prestige?

A face-up development costs one blue and grants a blue bonus. You have no blue bonus, no blue token and no gold. Can its own bonus make this purchase free? Separately, suppose you can pay for a white-bonus development and it gives you the final bonus needed by a noble: does that new bonus count for the noble at the end of this turn, or only next turn?

A card costs one blue and two green. You have four blue bonuses and no green bonuses. Can the three excess blue bonuses pay any green cost or give you blue tokens as change? What payment is still needed?

You qualify for two nobles and receive one. Before your next turn nobody acquires the other noble and your purchased cards stay unchanged. Were the bonuses used up by the first noble, and can taking gems on your next turn still lead to receiving the other noble? Can you collect that other noble during an opponent’s intervening turn?

You have no tokens, no purchased developments and no reserved cards. A face-up level-3 development is far too expensive for you to buy. May you reserve it anyway? Do you pay its printed cost when reserving, and do you take gold if available?

Instead of reserving a face-up card, you reserve the top card of the level-2 deck while twelve face-up market cards remain. Must any market card be removed or refilled because of that blind reservation, how many market cards remain, and can you take a second card as a replacement in your hand?

A level deck has run out, but its four face-up cards are still in the market. Must those cards be removed, or may they still be purchased or reserved? If one is purchased, what happens to that space and to the other three cards?

All development decks and face-up market cards have been exhausted; nobody has reached fifteen prestige. A player still has an affordable reserved card and gems are available in at least three colors. Does exhaustion itself end the game? May that player buy the reserved card or choose the three-different-gems action?

You already own ten tokens. Three different gem colors are available. Can you take one of each and then return all three newly taken tokens, ending with exactly the same token holdings? Is a net gain of tokens required?

The gold supply is empty. On A’s turn, A pays two gold while purchasing a card. B then reserves a card with fewer than three cards reserved. Are A’s spent gold tokens removed from the game, or can B take one, and how many gold tokens are left in the supply immediately after B’s reservation before any token-limit returns?
You have bought no level-1 or level-2 developments, but can pay for a face-up level-3 card. May you purchase that level-3 card now, or must you unlock its level by buying lower-level cards first?

You have twelve prestige, then purchase a three-prestige development whose bonus also makes you qualify for a noble. May you stop at fifteen and skip the noble visit? What is your total after your turn, and can the other players who still have a turn in the round continue playing?

Four players act A, B, C, D, with A first. D is the first player to reach fifteen prestige on D’s turn. Does A start another round, does everyone get one more turn, or is the game over after D completes this turn? Explain using equal turn counts.

In a two-player game, three nobles were revealed and the other seven removed during setup. After someone receives one noble, do you reveal a new tile from those seven to restore the display to three? Where does the acquired tile go and how many nobles remain available in the middle?
Match each component name to its color: emerald, diamond, sapphire, onyx, ruby and gold joker. How many development cards are in the box in total and at each of the three levels?

A card’s remaining cost after bonuses is one green. You hold both one green token and one gold. Must you spend green because you have it, or may you pay gold instead and keep the green? Where does the payment go?

Three gem piles contain one red, two blue and three green tokens. Other gem piles are empty. Can the three-different-gems action take one from each of these piles, or does the four-token minimum prohibit it? What would remain in those three piles?

You hold a gold token and want to exchange it directly for a red token in the supply without buying a development. Is that a listed action or a permitted use of the joker rule? What use does the summary give gold when purchasing?

On your turn you can legally buy a face-up card and can also take three different gems. You want neither benefit. May you simply pass without performing an action, or must you choose one of the four actions? This asks about voluntarily passing with legal actions available, not a state in which all actions are impossible.
